findings.title: Exclusive lock held across file and network I/O blocks all readers
findings.body: In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 GetWebAssets acquires entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock() with defer Unlock() and then performs disk I/O in readWebAssetsFromFile and potentially network I/O in readWebAssetsFromCDN while still holding the exclusive lock. Consequence is that every concurrent caller, including production fast-path readers that only need RLock to read the already-cached pointer, blocks for the duration of the file read and any HTTP fetch. During cold start this serializes the thundering herd and adds latency spikes; if CDN fetching is enabled a slow network stalls all page renders. The lock should only guard pointer publication: read outside the lock then Lock, re-check, and swap.

findings.title: Missing second cache check after acquiring write lock causes redundant reloads
findings.body: In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:45-48 GetWebAssets implements double-checked locking incorrectly: it checks entryPointAssetsCache under RLock, releases it, then takes the write Lock without re-checking. If two goroutines both observe nil (cold start) or race a Dev/Prod transition, both will sequentially execute readWebAssetsFromFile and the second overwrites the first. Consequence is N expensive manifest parses and file reads instead of one, plus possible inconsistency if the file changes between reads. After acquiring the write lock it should re-check if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil and return early.
